title: Atoms, stars and the universe
scope: Use your school’s topic list to select the ideas you need. These are original practice questions with illustrative values and suggested self-marking guidance, not official Cambridge papers.

objectives.label: Explain photon interactions using energy, frequency and intensity.
objectives.note: Use E = hf; distinguish energy per photon from photon arrival rate and explain a photoelectric threshold without abandoning wave evidence.

objectives.label: Distinguish nuclear radiation, irradiation and radioactive contamination.
objectives.note: Explain half-life as a statistical statement, compare alpha and gamma, and avoid generalising all exposures as radioactive contamination.

objectives.label: Explain fusion, fission and the mass–energy account of the Sun.
objectives.note: Use ΔE = Δmc² with system energy conserved; distinguish core nuclear fusion from surface burning and chemical combustion.

objectives.label: Use spectral lines as evidence about stellar composition and conditions.
objectives.note: Distinguish abundance from temperature effects on line strength and explain why several matching wavelengths are stronger evidence than one.

objectives.label: Explain how parallax and calibrated stellar brightness reveal distance.
objectives.note: Compare parallax angles, distinguish apparent from intrinsic brightness, and define a light-year as a distance.

objectives.label: Explain why stellar remnants depend on mass and physical support.
objectives.note: Describe a Sun-like star’s broad fate, distinguish white-dwarf support from continued fusion, and interpret a stability limit without a point-sized remnant.

objectives.label: Explain cosmological redshift and evidence for cosmic expansion.
objectives.note: Use stretching wavelength and changing separations, distinguish expansion from a central explosion, and connect redshift with complementary background-radiation evidence.
